paragraphs.text: Free, keyless web_search and web_fetch for the DeepSeek Harness.
# DeepSeek Harness - Web Tools
**Free, keyless `web_search` for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`).**

> **Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.1 or newer.** Works in both 0.2 surfaces: the web UI
> (profile `web`) and

DeepSeek's desktop app (profile `desktop`). The desktop
> app has no public download yet; it is bui

lt from DeepSeek's source.
>
> **Using dsh 0.1.x?** Use the `dsh-0.1` tag
> of the original repo thi

s project builds on (see
> Credits). Its instructions (`settings.yaml`, editing the installed
> `sta
ndard` preset) are for 0.1.0-rc.6 and do not apply to 0.2.

Every search provider `dsh` 0.2 ships needs an account: DeepSeek's own search
(a DeepSeek API key, o

r a DeepSeek-account sign-in), Exa, or Perplexity (their
API keys). If you run `dsh` against a local

model you may want none of that.
This repo is the keyless option.
## How it works

The plugin runs inside the `dsh` process and queries search engines directly.
It tries DuckDuckGo fi

rst, then Bing when DuckDuckGo is blocked, rate-limited,
or returns no results:

1. DuckDuckGo HTML
2. DuckDuckGo Lite
3. Bing RSS and Bing HTML, with and without market hints

Bing's fallback feed can return unrelated trending pages when it has no real
matches. The plugin sco

res every candidate against the query terms and discards
results that do not match. If no engine ret

urns anything relevant, the search
fails with an explicit `no relevant results` error instead of ret

urning
unrelated links.

There is no API key and no account in the default setup. Search traffic goes
from the `dsh` process
to fixed DuckDuckGo and Bing endpoints over HTTPS.

`web_fetch` needs nothing from this repo. DeepSeek ships
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-fetch-http` in the 0.

2 base bundle with fetch enabled (see
Security for what changed).

Everything here is upgrade-safe: it lives in your profile patch layer
(`cordis.patch.yml`) and `$DSH
_HOME`, not in shipped package files.

## Requirements

- `dsh` **0.2.0-rc.1+**. At the time of writing npm's `latest` tag still points
at 0.1.x, so install

the 0.2 line explicitly: `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@next`
- **Node** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`
- **pnp
m**: `dsh plugin` shells out to it (`npm i -g pnpm`)
## Plugin panel (0.2.1-rc.3+)

> **2.0.0** is the rename release — the package is `@residenthiago/dsh-web-tools`
> (previously `dsh

-plugin-ddg-search``dsh-0.1`). Update profile manifests
> accordingly: the dependency key, `dsh.prof

ile.bundles` entry and the
> bundle row's `name:`; the loader row id stays `web-search-ddg`.

On dsh 0.2.1-rc.3+ the plugin is a **bundle** (`dsh.bundle.patch` in its
`package.json`), so the Plu

gins panel lists it under **Personal** as
**"Web Tools"** (zh: Web 工具; display name from `plugin/loc

ale/en|zh.json`,
`meta.title`) with the standard enable/disable toggle — enabled it writes
`"@reside

nthiago/dsh-web-tools"` into the profile manifest's
`dsh.profile.bundles`. In that flow the `- inser

t: id: web-search-ddg` row
comes from the bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml`; do **not** also copy that

row
into the profile patch (duplicate ids conflict). The `- id: web` row from
step 2 is still yours
to keep — it belongs to the web seam, not this package.
## Install
### 1. The plugin, per profile

The easiest path is a tarball release through the Plugins panel (**Plugins →
Add plugin** → paste
`h
ttps://github.com/residenthiago2011/DSH-Web-Tools/releases/download/v2.0.0/residenthiago-dsh-web-too

ls-2.0.0.tgz`
— see the
Releases page
for the newest tag). The panel records the install in the prof

ile manifest,
and the bundle patch rows below are then composed automatically. Manual local
install:

Plugins resolve from the **profile** directory, so install into each profile you
use. `web` is the b

rowser UI, `desktop` is DeepSeek's desktop app, `headless` is
one-shot `dsh headless "task"` runs:

### 2. Wire it up in `cordis.patch.yml`

On 0.2 all configuration lives in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`
(default `$DSH_HOM

E` is `~/.dsh`); `settings.yaml` is gone. Add these rows to
the file of every profile from step 1 (f

ull commented copy:
examples/cordis.patch.yml):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A patch replaces the `web` row's whole config, so `fetchProvider` is restated
even though it is the

es the `web` row's whole config, so `fetchProvider` is restated
even though it is the shipped value.

No agent-preset change is needed: 0.2's shipped `standard` preset already
exposes both `web_search`

and `web_fetch` to the model. If you use a custom
preset row, keep its `tool-web` row.
### 3. Restart

- **Web UI:** stop `dsh web` and start it again.
- **Desktop app:** quit it fully and reopen it.

Then start a **new session**; a session that was already open keeps its old
tool catalog.
### Upgrading from 1.0

The provider ID is unchanged. 2.0.0 removed the legacy `baseURL` shim option:
any `baseURL` left in

the config is ignored and the plugin always searches
directly. To clean up:

## Security

**Search results are untrusted input.** Treat titles, snippets, and fetched pages
as data, not instr

uctions. A malicious result can contain prompt-injection text.
Do not run unattended agents with bro
ad tool access unless you accept that risk.

**Direct search sends queries to DuckDuckGo and Bing.** The default provider
contacts only fixed sea

rch endpoints; it does not fetch arbitrary URLs. It does
send your query text to those services, so
do not search for secrets.

**`web_fetch` is on by default in 0.2, and its provider changed.** The 0.1-era
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web

-fetch-http` had no SSRF protection, which is why DeepSeek
shipped fetch disabled back then. The 0.2

provider, per its own README, accepts
only public HTTP(S) destinations: it resolves each host, reje

cts the request if
any address is not public (loopback, LAN, and most VPN/tailnet ranges), pins
the

connection to the validated addresses, and blocks cross-origin redirects.
It still cannot stop a mod

el from sending data *to* a public URL, so think
twice before running an unattended agent with fetch

rom sending data *to* a public URL, so think
twice before running an unattended agent with fetch on.
